domain.description: Two carriers and two primitives of different kinds. Nine sites are arranged so that each site is adjacent to exactly two others around a single closed corridor, and every site lies in exactly one of three districts, each district being a run of three consecutive sites.
domain.name: a finite ring corridor of nine sites carrying a declared district map
domain.source_semantics: The adjacent relation states which sites are immediate neighbours along the corridor. The district operation states which district each site lies in. The identifiers are opaque names carrying no declared arithmetic; both primitives are declared extensionally.
domain.why_two_primitives: 017.26b section 5 requires a Strong positive to rest on a fixture whose useful invariance arises from JOINT preservation of more than one typed primitive. Here the adjacent relation constrains local neighbour structure and the district operation constrains a global three-fold block structure, and neither is recoverable from the other. The joint-load-bearing test in section 5 is executed mechanically against this schema, not asserted.
domain.would_these_facts_belong_without_any_mod: Yes. Which sites neighbour which, and which administrative district each site lies in, are ordinary facts about a physical corridor. A surveyor would record both whether or not anyone ever fitted a model to anything.

independence_fence: This schema is a self-contained abstract corridor. It reuses no catalogue, corpus, hidden label, or learning target, and it is not a renaming of the fixture A incidence relation: it has different carrier cardinalities, a different admitted-input cardinality, and a primitive of a different kind.
